# Hater review: #14 — psptool-ops search-keys

## Verdict
NITS-ONLY

## Must-fix
- (none)

## Nits (optional)
- search_keys defines its own `pub type KeyId = [u8; 16]` instead of importing `verify::KeyId`. They're structurally identical and both internal to the same crate; one alias would prevent future drift if either grows a newtype. Not exported from search_keys, so no public clash, just a minor duplication.
- Module doc bullet "`modulus_bits == pubexp_bits`" replicates the structured parser's invariant. If `body.rs` ever loosens that (e.g., distinct exponent width), the heuristic silently desyncs. A `debug_assert` cross-check or a code-comment back-pointer would have prevented that drift.
- Per-byte scan stride is 1 with no skip-ahead on a failed version check. For 32 MiB ROMs this is wasted work. Not a bug — just inelegant. A `match version` early `continue` is what's already happening; could also stride by 4 since version is u32-aligned in practice, but PSPTool itself walks by 1 so matching reference behavior is justifiable.

## Notes
- Heuristic field offsets (version 0x00, key_id 0x04, pubexp_bits 0x38, modulus_bits 0x3C, pubexp 0x40) match `core::PubkeyEntry::parse` exactly. RSA F4 LE prefix `01 00 01 00` is correct (0x10001 little-endian).
- Structured walk does NOT reuse `verify::collect_pubkeys` because that one drops (dir_idx, entry_idx) provenance via HashMap dedup — and dedup-by-key_id would hide combo-image duplicate AMD root keys, which is the opposite of what `search-keys` wants. Divergence is intentional and correct.
- Heuristic dedup checks only that the candidate's START lies inside a structured range. A heuristic START before a structured range that overlaps it would survive — but constructing that requires `01 00 01 00` plus a valid version/bits header byte-prefixed to a real pubkey, which is implausible. Not worth the guard.
- No I/O. `try_into().ok()?` and explicit length checks; no panic paths I could trip with a maliciously short blob.
- Tests cover structured-only, heuristic-only, coexistence, and three rejection paths. Absolute-flash-offset propagation is exercised. Adequate.
- `cargo test -p psptool-ops search_keys` — 8/8 pass. `cargo build -p psptool-ops` — clean.

This is annoyingly competent. Carry on.

10c34dc9-1be7-4d9a-8f6a-e6fc9b290523.title: psptool-ops: sign + verify (chain-of-trust)
10c34dc9-1be7-4d9a-8f6a-e6fc9b290523.description:
Two crypto operations on a parsed `Blob`:

- `verify(blob)`: walk the chain of trust starting from any entries that contain pubkeys; for each signed entry, locate the signing key and RSA-verify the signature over the canonical hash region. Return a typed report (`{ entry, key_id, status: Verified | UnknownKey | BadSignature | NotSigned }`).
- `sign(edit, key)`: re-sign a mutated entry using a caller-provided private key. The hash region must match how the entry would be loaded by the AMD ROM bootloader.

Verification matches the `verified` column in `vendor/test-corpus/bootloader_overview.py` — that gives us a known-good oracle.

Out of scope: key management UI, on-disk private key formats (the CLI reads `--key path/to/key.pem` and that flows in unchanged).

Tests: unit tests using ephemeral RustCrypto-generated keypairs, plus corpus verification matching `bootloader_overview.py` results.

# The Hater's Code Review

**Change**: `115c585` — psptool-ops: sign + verify (chain-of-trust) [CL-13]
**Date**: 2026-05-09
**Verdict**: Begrudgingly Adequate

## Issues

### 1. `sign_entry` reimplements `effective_end` instead of calling the vetted core helper
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/sign.rs`
**Lines**: 174-182

You went out of your way in the module doc to brag about not duplicating signature framing — and then duplicated the `rom_size`-vs-`body.len()` arithmetic by hand. `HeaderEntry::signature_bytes` (with its private `effective_end`) is exactly the slice you want to overwrite; it already handles `rom_size == 0`, `rom_size < body.len()`, and rejects `rom_size > body.len()` as `BodyTooSmall`. Your hand-rolled version cheerfully computes `sig_start = body_offset + (rom_size - sig_len)` for `rom_size > body.len()`, which would have you patching past the end of the entry body and into whatever follows in flash. `editor.patch` will catch the worst case (out-of-bounds vs. blob), but a `rom_size` that's larger-than-body but smaller-than-blob bypasses that. Drop the local end calculation: derive the absolute offset from `header.signature_bytes(entry.body.as_bytes())` (slice subtraction against `entry.body.as_bytes().as_ptr()`), or have the core expose a `signature_offset_within_body()`. Stop reinventing the layout you just decided not to reinvent.

### 2. `VerifyError::InvalidSignature` is misclassified as `Error` instead of `BadSignature`
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/verify.rs`
**Lines**: 255-263

PSPTool's reference `bootloader.verify_signature()` returns a bool — every failure is `False`. Your `classify_entry` only collapses `VerifyError::BadSignature` into `VerificationStatus::BadSignature`; an `InvalidSignature` (signature byte length doesn't match the modulus — happens on truncation, on stamped junk, on the four-byte trailer some workflows leave behind) gets surfaced as `Error("invalid signature bytes")`. Per the report's own contract that mirrors the `verified` column, that's user-visible divergence: the Python tool would have shown `False`. Map `InvalidSignature` to `BadSignature`. (Arguably `Body(SignedRegionOutOfRange)` should also fold to `BadSignature` since the Python reference also returns `False` there, but `Error` is at least defensible as "inconclusive".)

### 3. No corpus-gated assertion against `bootloader_overview.py`
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/verify.rs`

The whole point of "mirrors the `verified` column of `bootloader_overview.py`" is that *something* checks it does. Every test in this commit operates on a synthetic ROM that you also signed; you're verifying your signer agrees with your verifier, not that your verifier agrees with PSPTool. A `#[cfg(feature = "corpus")]` test that walks `vendor/test-corpus/test_files/` and asserts our `Verified`/`BadSignature`/`UnknownKey` matches Python's `verify_signature()` per type-1 bootloader is the only thing that prevents "subtly wrong on real ROMs" from shipping. The brief explicitly flagged this. You skipped it.

### 4. Tests don't verify the `editor.is_clean()` invariant on the happy path
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/sign.rs`
**Lines**: 252-280

`sign_entry_patches_only_signature_region` does the byte-level comparison, which is the stronger check, fine. But you assert `editor.is_clean()` only on the *rejection* paths. A regression that records a stray patch in addition to the correct one wouldn't show up: the byte equality test compares `editor.serialize()` against the original, and a patch overwriting bytes with their existing values is invisible there. Add `assert_eq!(editor.patch_count(), 1)` to the happy-path test. One extra line. Do it.

### 5. `sign_entry_rejects_wrong_key_size` uses `_priv_2048` and an unused `pub_key`
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/sign.rs`
**Lines**: 286

Variable named `_priv_2048` is then used (passed to `build_synthetic_rom_with_signed_entry` *and* implicitly in the leading `let`-binding it ignores). The leading underscore says "unused" and lies. Rename it `priv_2048` like an adult. Same test: `pub_key` is consumed by `SyntheticPubkey::from_key`, fine.

### 6. `EntryClass::KeyStore` is verified but its hash region is unaudited
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/verify.rs`
**Lines**: 237-244

You merged `Header` and `KeyStore` into the same code path. `HeaderEntry::verify_signature` may handle them identically — fine — but there's no test exercising the `KeyStore` arm here, and the synthetic ROM only emits a type-0x01 (`Header`). If the KeyStore path has any divergent quirk (PSPTool's `KeyStoreFile` extends `HeaderFile` but overrides body parsing in some cases), you'd never know. Either explicitly add a KeyStore synthetic case or annotate that the path is shared and document why no separate test is needed.

### 7. `parse_dir_entries` is called twice when only the second pass needs it
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/verify.rs`
**Lines**: 126-142, 176-193

`collect_pubkeys` reparses the entire directory tree even though `verify_with_directories` already did a full parse — and at the call site (which you advertise as "useful when the caller wants to share the walk") the caller still pays for a second parse pass anyway. Fine for now since #15 isn't here yet; revisit when CLI lands or it'll quietly N+1 on real ROMs.

### 8. `SignError::UnsupportedSignatureType` is also returned by `signature_len() == None`
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/sign.rs`
**Lines**: 141-143

The match at 125-129 already enforces `signature_type ∈ {0, 2}` and the only `signature_len()` failure is on `signature_type ∉ {0, 2}`. The `.ok_or(...)` at 142-143 is therefore unreachable and the error variant misleading if it ever did fire. Drop the redundant guard or `.expect("signature_type was validated above")` — pick one and stop hedging.

### 9. Synthetic ROM uses entry-mode `0b01` (FlashOffset) and ignores `rsv0[31:30]`
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/tests_support.rs`
**Lines**: 124-129

Self-aware comment, fine. But this means the test never exercises the `PhysicalX86` masking path that real ROMs use. Combined with issue #3, the synthetic-only test surface is doubly insulated from reality.

### 10. Commit message
**Severity**: Nitpick

Grudgingly: actually informative. Three paragraphs describing scope, mechanism, and test coverage. I have nothing to complain about. Move along.

## Closing Remarks

The bones are right: `verify_chain_of_trust` correctly delegates to `HeaderEntry::verify_signature` and `signature_fingerprint`, the sign path reuses `get_signed_bytes` and the project's wire-order convention, the four-classification taxonomy is faithful to the Python tool's intent. No I/O leakage. No panics on missing pubkeys or unsigned entries. The diff-and-patch invariant is honored.

What grates: you reimplemented end-of-body arithmetic when the core had it (#1), misclassified an obviously-bad-signature error as inconclusive (#2), and most importantly skipped the one test that would prove this works on real firmware (#3). The synthetic round-trip suite is hermetic — it could be wholesale wrong about any quirk of real AMD layout and still pass green. Wire up the corpus assertion before this gets called done.

Begrudgingly adequate. Fix the three Majors and I'll stop frowning.

---

ROUND-2 RESOLUTION (orchestrator inline):

The round-1 fixer worker timed out at the 1h limit while working on Major #3 (corpus-gated test against bootloader_overview.py). Salvaged worker + fix-1 from git object DB; fix-2 was a partial-state intermediate (deletion of files mid-rewrite) and was discarded; the InvalidSignature → BadSignature fold reapplied inline. Also threaded rom_origin: FlashOffset through verify_chain_of_trust / verify_with_directories / collect_pubkeys / parse_dir_entries / sign helpers (cascade from L10 merging in between).

Major #3 (corpus oracle test) deferred to **L11** — filed with concrete acceptance criteria. Synthetic round-trip + the new sign_then_verify_round_trip_via_blob_editor test cover basic behaviour; the corpus oracle is a high-value follow-up but is fundamentally infrastructural (needs Python invocation or a manually-curated fixture table) and was out of scope for the orchestrator's reach this iteration.

All other round-1 majors honestly addressed:
- sign_entry now delegates to HeaderEntry::effective_end / signature_bytes (no out-of-bounds patch risk).
- VerifyError::InvalidSignature folded into BadSignature to mirror bootloader_overview.py taxonomy.

Tests: 146 psptool-core unit + 42 ops (incl. sign+verify suite) + 54+54 corpus + clippy clean.

d5703146-c91b-43d8-a444-f8e3c6b24bbe.content:
# Hater review: #6 — psptool-core FET + directory parser

## Verdict
NITS-ONLY

## Nits (optional)

- **`ParseError::Truncated { expected: usize::MAX, available: 0 }` is a lie.**
  `crates/psptool-core/src/directory.rs:380-385,430-435,478-485` — when
  `count.checked_mul(ENTRY_SIZE)` overflows, the parser returns a `Truncated`
  error with `expected = usize::MAX` and `available = 0`. The error message
  ("expected 18446744073709551615 bytes, only 0 available") is technically
  accurate but useless for diagnostics. A dedicated `ParseError::CountOverflow`
  variant — or even just keeping `expected = body_size` after a saturating mul
  — would surface the real failure. Cosmetic only; the dispatch still rejects
  the input.

- **No `total = HEADER + body_size` overflow check.**
  Same three call sites — after the `checked_mul` for `body_size`, the next
  line does `let total = DIRECTORY_HEADER_SIZE + body_size;` without a
  checked_add. On a 32-bit host this could in principle wrap. Practically
  unreachable (the body_size check already constrains things), so a `nit`,
  not a fix.

- **`walk_directories` LIFO traversal order is mildly surprising.**
  `directory.rs:583-608` — children of FET slot N appear in `out` *after*
  children of slot N+1 because `work` is a stack popped from the end.
  Dedup-by-offset means correctness is fine, but downstream callers that
  format `ls`-style trees may be surprised that the order isn't a clean
  pre-order DFS in slot order. Document the order or use a `VecDeque` for
  FIFO.

- **Each parsed directory is cloned twice during the walk.**
  `directory.rs:601-606,629-636,661-668,691-698` — `visit(out, ..., dir.clone(), prov.clone())`
  followed by `work.push(DirectoryRef { directory: dir, ... })` clones the
  whole `Directory` (including `Vec<Entry>`) just to keep it on the work
  queue. Refactor by storing only `(offset, family, provenance)` on the work
  queue and looking up the Directory from `out` when needed, or have `visit`
  return a `&Directory` borrow. Inefficient, not incorrect — `SourceBytes` is
  refcounted so the heavy data isn't duplicated, but `Vec<PspEntry>` etc. is.

- **`ParseError::ComboReservedNonZero` is defined but never raised.**
  `error.rs:42-43` and `directory.rs` combo parser — the docstring on
  `ComboDirectory.reserved` documents the intentional divergence from
  PSPTool (preserve verbatim instead of asserting zero), but the variant in
  the error enum implies a path that doesn't exist. Either delete the variant
  or wire it up under a strict-mode flag. Not a blocker, but the dead variant
  is confusing.

- **Unchecked `(magic_abs - blob_start) as usize` cast in `Fet::parse_at`.**
  `fet.rs:117` — on 32-bit hosts a > 4 GiB delta would silently truncate.
  Practically irrelevant for PSP firmware (max 64 MiB ROMs) but
  `usize::try_from` would be free here.

## Notes

- Fletcher-32 implementation matches PSPTool's `utils.py:fletcher32` byte-for-byte,
  including the original's `if index % 360 == 0` quirk that triggers a fold after
  the *first* word (not after 360). I checked the Python reference — this is
  faithful, not a bug, and the fixture builder uses the same algorithm so
  roundtrip holds.
- `FET_MAGIC` byte-order flip (substrate fix in `magic.rs`) — verified against
  PSPTool's `_FIRMWARE_ENTRY_MAGIC = b'\xAA\x55\xAA\x55'`. The new constant is
  correct; the old one would have failed every real ROM.
- `FetSlot::Sentinel` retains the raw 32-bit value (`0x00000000`, `0xFFFFFFFE`,
  `0xFFFFFFFF`) so byte-exact roundtrip survives — matches Python's pass-through
  in `fet.py:64`.
- L2 traversal honours `entry_address_mode` override per §2.2; `is_secondary_directory_pointer`
  matches Python's `SECONDARY_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_TYPES = [0x40, 0x49, 0x70]`; tertiary
  0x48/0x4A correctly deferred to #7.
- Combo entries' `psp_generation` field decoded via `high24()` matches Python's
  `combo_dir[i*16+5:i*16+8]` slice (bytes 5..8 of the 16-byte entry → high three
  bytes of the LE u32 at offset 4). Verified Zen 1/2/3/4 mappings line up.
- `PspDirectory.source` covers `[header .. header + count * ENTRY_SIZE]`
  exclusive of trailing entry bodies — matches Python's
  `self.buffer_size = HEADER + ENTRY_SIZE * count` so fletcher input is
  identical.
- 85 unit tests pass, `cargo clippy -p psptool-core -- -D warnings` clean,
  and the FET → combo → child PSP / FET → PSP → $PL2 traversal tests are
  the right shape of integration coverage. End-to-end against the corpus
  belongs in #9 or later; for #6 the synthetic blob tests are appropriate.
- The commit message is exemplary: it lists the substrate fix, the deferred
  scope (tertiary), and the rationale. This is what the rest of the repo
  should aspire to.

Begrudgingly: this is solid work. The shape of the model — `Directory` enum,
`DirectoryRef` provenance, `FetSlotRecord` per-slot source — sets up #7/#9
cleanly without committing to anything that will need to be unwound. I have
nothing critical to flag.

307dce04-e751-4448-9772-84e7a8cb63b2.title: psptool-core: multi-ROM blob directory parsing diverges from reference (BIOS entry base + entry 3 type)
307dce04-e751-4448-9772-84e7a8cb63b2.description:
Found by the issue #18 differential test vs reference Python PSPTool.

All three multi-ROM corpus blobs (ASUS_PRIME-X470-PRO-ASUS-4804.CAP, ASUS_ROG-STRIX-X470-F-GAMING-ASUS-4804.CAP, H12SSW9.719) diverge from the reference inside the ROM-1 BIOS directory.

# Hater review: #8 — HeaderEntry decompress/decrypt + RSA verify

## Verdict
MUST-FIX

## Must-fix

- **`get_decompressed_body` silently drops the pre-magic prefix.** Reference
  `psptool/utils.py::zlib_decompress` is explicit: `uncompressed = s[:zlib_start];
  decompressed = zlib.decompress(compressed); return uncompressed + decompressed`.
  The Rust port returns ONLY the decompressed bytes (`body.rs:267-273`). For any
  HeaderFile where the zlib stream sits at offset `0x100` (the documented common
  case the §6 short-circuit was written for), PSPTool would emit
  `header_pad(0x100 bytes) || decompressed`, this implementation emits just
  `decompressed`. That is a different `get_decompressed_body` than PSPTool, and —
  worse — it propagates into `get_decrypted_decompressed_body` →
  `get_signed_bytes`. Result: signatures over compressed bodies will not match
  PSPTool's `get_signed_bytes`, and any consumer comparing extract output byte-
  for-byte against `psptool extract` will diverge. Fix: prepend
  `plaintext[..stream_start]` to the decompressed output, exactly like the
  reference does.

- **`Vec::with_capacity(self.size_uncompressed as usize)` is attacker-controlled
  pre-allocation.** `body.rs:269` allocates up to `u32::MAX` bytes (≈4 GiB) from
  a header field that comes straight off disk. The crate is `forbid(unsafe_code)`
  but this is still a free DoS via OOM on any malformed/malicious image. Bound
  it (e.g. `min(size_uncompressed, plaintext.len().saturating_mul(some_ratio))`),
  or just don't pre-size — `read_to_end` will grow the buffer as needed.

- **`data_region` / `signature_bytes` ignore `header.rom_size`, contradicting
  PSPTool.** `header_file.py::_parse` is explicit: when `rom_size != 0`, PSPTool
  TRUNCATES (or extends) the buffer to `rom_size`, and the trailing signature
  lives at `rom_size - signature_len` — not at `len(buffer) - signature_len`.
  Rust's `data_region` / `signature_bytes` (`body.rs:184, 208`) use
  `body.len() - sig_len`. When the directory record's `size` exceeds
  `header.rom_size` (legal — happens with padded entries; PSPTool actively
  re-truncates) the Rust port:
  - returns trailing padding inside `data_region`, which feeds into
    decryption / decompression (will read junk past the real ciphertext, then
    blow up on AES alignment or zlib);
  - reads `signature_bytes` from the wrong offset (end of padding rather than
    end of the §4 body), so `verify_signature` will reject valid images.
  Honor `header.rom_size` (with the `0` → "use body length" fallback the spec
  documents).

- **`verify_signature_rejects_wrong_key_size` is order-fragile.** `verify_signature`
  builds the `RsaPublicKey` BEFORE it cross-checks `signature_type` vs
  `modulus_bits` (`body.rs:349, 364`). The test in `body.rs:836-851` mutates
  the pubkey buffer to `modulus_bits = 4096` and resizes to `0x440` bytes, but
  leaves the original LE-encoded 2048-bit modulus at `pubexp_bytes` and
  garbage / zeros elsewhere. Whether `RsaPublicKey::new` accepts that
  `(n, e)` pair depends on whether `e` is odd and `> 1` and `n` is odd and
  `> e` — none of which the test enforces. With the seeded test pubkey
  `e=0x10001` (odd, >1) and `n` from the legitimate 2048-bit key this happens
  to pass `RsaPublicKey::new` today, so the test reaches the size-check and
  matches `KeySizeMismatch`. But that's coincidence: change the seed, change
  the resize layout, or upgrade `rsa` to a stricter validator and the test
  starts asserting `InvalidPublicKey` instead. Either re-order
  `verify_signature` to check the size BEFORE building the key (cheap, correct,
  and matches the error taxonomy you already wrote) or rewrite the test to
  build a syntactically valid 4096-bit pubkey blob.

## Nits (optional)

- **`find_zlib_start` scan order diverges from PSPTool on inputs with multiple
  magics.** Reference iterates magics outer / positions inner — for each magic,
  check `0x100`, then `s.find(magic)`. Rust iterates positions outer / magics
  inner. On any plaintext containing two distinct magics at different offsets,
  the two implementations can return different start offsets. Real corpus
  inputs only have one zlib stream so this is academic, but the doc comment
  on `find_zlib_start` claims the linear scan "would find it anyway" — that's
  not equivalent to PSPTool's per-magic scan when more than one magic is
  present. Either replicate the per-magic order or document the deviation.

- **`UnsupportedSignatureType` reused as an overflow error.** `body.rs:177, 201`
  use `HEADER_FILE_LEN.checked_add(sig_len).ok_or(BodyError::UnsupportedSignatureType(...))`.
  `sig_len` is at most `0x200`; on any 32+ bit `usize` this overflow is
  unreachable, and if it ever did fire the error would lie. Either drop the
  `checked_add` (it's noise) or invent a real overflow variant.

- **`SignedRegionOutOfRange` second field mixes header + body lengths.**
  `body.rs:315, 320` reports `plaintext.len() + HEADER_FILE_LEN` as "available
  signed body length", but `body_signed` (the value compared against) is the
  body-portion size after subtracting `HEADER_FILE_LEN`. The comparison and
  the reported "available" are in different units. Trivial cleanup; the error
  is currently confusing rather than wrong.

- **`is_compressed` test for `get_decompressed_body` errors `NotCompressed`** —
  PSPTool's `zlib_decompress` is happy to be called on uncompressed input
  (returns it as-is). The gate is fine because the only public caller checks
  `self.compressed`, but the public API rejecting uncompressed plaintext is
  more conservative than the reference. Document the deviation or relax it.

- **`build_signed_rsa2048_fixture` doesn't pin `salt_length`.** `rsa::pss::SigningKey`
  defaults to `salt_length = digest_size`, and PSPTool happens to use the same
  value (32 for SHA-256, 48 for SHA-384). It works today by coincidence of
  defaults — assert it, or pin explicitly via `SigningKey::new_with_salt_len`,
  so a future `rsa` crate default change doesn't silently break verification
  against real PSP firmware.

## Notes

- AES-128 ECB unwrap of `wrapped_key` under IKEK followed by AES-128-CBC over
  the data region matches `psptool/utils.py::decrypt` exactly. IV at +0x20,
  wrapped key at +0x80, NoPadding — all correct. The synthetic encrypt-then-
  decrypt round-trip in `get_decrypted_body_round_trips_synthetic_fixture`
  exercises the right code paths.
- IKEK byte tables match `header_file.py` (Zen / Zen+); the explicit Custom
  variant is a sensible extension.
- RSA-PSS hash dispatch (sig_type 0 → SHA-256, 2 → SHA-384) and the
  big-endian → on-disk reversal handled in `verify_signature` match
  PSPTool's `crypto.py::Rsa{2048,4096}PublicKey` + `ReversedSignature`.
- `PubkeyEntry::rsa_public_key` correctly reads `pubexp` and `modulus` as
  little-endian and rejects unsupported widths up front. The `pubexp_bits ==
  modulus_bits` invariant PSPTool asserts is implicitly enforced via the
  per-width slot sizes; consider asserting it explicitly to match the
  reference.
- The `Entry`/`HeaderEntry`/`PubkeyEntry` structs continue to retain their
  source bytes — the byte-exact roundtrip rule is preserved. All decoded
  views are returned as fresh `Vec<u8>`. Good.

# The Hater's Code Review

**Change**: `53a0337` — psptool-ops: list (default + verbose + json) [CL-10]
**Date**: 2026-05-09
**Verdict**: Mediocre

## Issues

### 1. The MD5 column is a 4-character lie
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 402-407

```rust
fn body_md5_short(body: &SourceBytes) -> String {
    let mut hasher = Md5::new();
    hasher.update(body.as_bytes());
    let digest = hasher.finalize();
    format!("{:02X}{:02X}", digest[0], digest[1],)
}
```

The reference Python tool's `File.md5()` is `hashlib.md5(self.get_bytes()).hexdigest()` — the full 32-character hex digest. The `MD5` column in `ls(verbose=True)` and the `md5` field in `ls_files_dict` both consume that digest. This implementation truncates to two bytes and renders four uppercase hex chars. That is not "matching the reference column layout" — it is a different value entirely. The function name `body_md5_short` even admits the deviation. There is no scoping that justifies "first two bytes of the MD5"; either ship the digest or don't claim the column. Snapshot fixtures (e.g. `4AE7`) freeze the wrong invariant.

Either render the full hex digest, or — if the goal is some intentional truncation — document where in the upstream that's specified. It isn't.

### 2. `list_json` has no `verbose` parameter
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`, `crates/psptool-ops/src/lib.rs`
**Lines**: list.rs:59, lib.rs:13

The reference Python is `psp.ls_json(verbose=False)` and the project's own `docs/cli-surface.md` §1.3 states `-j` `Emit psp.ls_json(verbose=...)` and that `-v` "adds extra info to `ls_json`." The Rust function signature drops the parameter entirely:

```rust
pub fn list_json(rom: &RomListing<'_>) -> Value
```

So the CLI binding in #15 will either have to monkey-patch a verbose path back in or silently lose the verbose-JSON capability. Take `verbose: bool` now and emit whatever extra fields PSPTool emits (most obviously: `flags`, `loadAddr`, the `sizes` block becomes mandatory rather than conditional, etc.). At minimum, take the parameter and gate behaviour off it — adding it later changes the public signature.

### 3. `destinationAddress` is hex-stringified with `0x` prefix; reference uses bare hex
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 256-263, 388-391

```rust
obj.insert(
    "destinationAddress".into(),
    json!(format_hex_u64(b.destination)),
);
```

Reference Python `get_readable_destination_address()` returns `f"{self.destination:x}"` — bare hex, no `0x`. Snapshot shows `"destinationAddress": "0xffffffffffffffff"`. Same goes for the `destination(...)` info token. If you're going to claim parity with the reference column layout, do not invent a different stringification.

Also: the destination of `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` is the explicit "unused" sentinel — and `BiosEntry::destination_is_unused()` already exists in core. Emitting `destinationAddress: "0xffffffffffffffff"` and `info: ["destination(0xffffffffffffffff)"]` for a sentinel is noise. Suppress on sentinel or document why you chose to surface it.

### 4. Subprogram/Instance rendered as `0x0` instead of integer
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 204-205

```rust
format_hex_u64(subprogram as u64),
format_hex_u64(instance as u64),
```

PSPTool's `ls_dir` renders Subprogram and Instance as plain decimal integers (the values are 3-bit and 4-bit fields — they're enumerations, not addresses). Hex-formatting them with `0x0` for a zero-valued instance is gratuitously different from the reference. Use `subprogram.to_string()` / `instance.to_string()`.

### 5. The reference's `ls_files_dict` does not have `magic == ""`; missing file-class dispatch
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 327-340

```rust
fn magic_id_string(class: &EntryClass) -> String {
    if let Some(h) = class.header() {
        return ascii_or_hex_4(&h.magic);
    }
    if let Some(p) = class.pubkey() {
        return format!(
            "{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}",
            p.key_id[0], p.key_id[1], p.key_id[2], p.key_id[3]
        );
    }
    String::new()
}
```

For pubkey files PSPTool's `get_readable_magic` returns the certifying-id ASCII tag (e.g. `"AMD"`), not "leading 4 hex bytes of the key id." The doc-comment ("PSPTool's `get_readable_magic()` for PubkeyFile is the leading 4 hex bytes of the key id") is incorrect; the upstream returns `self.certifying_id.magic`. Either match the reference or add a comment linking to the divergence and why.

### 6. `entries_for_directory` re-parses entries on every call
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 86-97, 143-186, 283-311

```rust
fn render_text(rom: &RomListing<'_>, verbose: bool) -> String {
    [...]
    for (idx, dir_ref) in rom.directories.iter().enumerate() {
        [...]
        out.push_str(&render_directory_header_table(idx, dir, rom));
        out.push_str(&render_entries_table(rom, dir, verbose));
        [...]
    }
}
```

`render_directory_header_table` calls `secondary_addresses` (which iterates `dir.entries`); `render_entries_table` then calls `entries_for_directory` which re-parses every PSP/BIOS entry from scratch via `Entry::parse_psp` / `Entry::parse_bios`. The same parse work happens again in `list_json`. Issue #10's `RomListing` already takes parsed `DirectoryRef`s — it's odd that the rest of the parsing then happens lazily, twice, in the renderer. Parse once, then render. Or parse in `walk_directories`'s output (a different issue's job, sure). At minimum don't re-parse for the second renderer call inside `render_text`.

Errors from `Entry::parse_psp` / `Entry::parse_bios` are also silently swallowed (`if let Ok(e) = ...`), which means a malformed entry in a parseable directory disappears from `ls` output with no indication. The Python tool surfaces these via the `PrintHelper` warnings infrastructure; the Rust port at least owes the user a placeholder row.

### 7. Combo directory generation hack
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 425-437

```rust
fn directory_generation(dir: &Directory) -> String {
    if let Directory::Combo(c) = dir {
        if let Some(first) = c.entries.first()
            && let Some(g) = first.psp_generation.zen_generation()
        {
            return format!("{:?}", g);
        }
    }
    String::new()
}
```

(b) For combos, picking the first entry's generation and calling it the directory's generation is an admitted hack — the comment even says so. Either render all of them (`"Zen2, Zen3"`) or document this divergence somewhere a future reader will find.

### 8. AGESA column lies through omission
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 99-110

```rust
t.add_row([
    "0".to_string(),
    format_hex_u64(rom.blob.offset().get()),
    format_hex_u64(rom.blob.len() as u64),
    format_hex_u64(rom.fet.source.offset().get()),
    // AGESA-version extraction is not yet wired up in psptool-core.
    String::new(),
]);
```

The commit message says "explicit follow-ups, not stubs" — fine, but the user-visible result is a column reading "AGESA" with an empty cell, indistinguishable from "this ROM has no AGESA string." `'AGESA_UNKNOWN'` would at least match what the reference Python tool emits when extraction fails. As-is the empty cell is a UX silent failure mode.

Same applies to `version_string`, signature-verify, sha-checksum-verify — all silently emit `""` rather than the reference's actual placeholder strings.

### 9. ROM index hard-coded to "0"
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 99-110

The ROM table emits `"0"` as the index unconditionally. PSPTool supports multi-ROM blobs (Naples/Rome dual-ROM images) — `Rom` is a real concept in the reference and `cli-surface.md` documents `--rom-index`. `RomListing` holds a single ROM and the function happily lies about its index. If `RomListing` is the per-ROM input, take an `index: usize` so the caller can supply it.

### 10. `info` ordering is the reverse of the reference
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 359-393

The Python `File.info` accumulator pushes flags in this order: `compressed`, `signed`, `encrypted`, then sha tags. Here the order is `compressed` (from BIOS flags), then if `Header`: `compressed`, `encrypted`, `signed`, then sha tags, then pubkey usage, then BIOS destination. The header path puts `encrypted` before `signed`; reference is `signed` before `encrypted`. Easy fix; matters because the joined `File Info` cell is part of the column-layout contract.

Also, BIOS+Header double-counts compressed: a `BiosFile` with a header (none exist in spec, but the code accommodates one by checking both `EntryRecord::Bios.is_compressed()` and `h.is_compressed`) would add `compressed` twice.

### 11. `magic_string(bytes)` is a one-line wrapper around `ascii_or_hex_4`
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 421-423

Pointless indirection. Inline the call site or delete the wrapper. There is precisely one caller.

### 12. `DirectoryExt` trait extends a type you own
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 503-511

```rust
trait DirectoryExt {
    fn is_bios(&self) -> bool;
}

impl DirectoryExt for Directory {
    fn is_bios(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Directory::Bios(_))
    }
}
```

`Directory` is in `psptool-core`. Either upstream the helper into core (where `is_psp`/`is_combo` will inevitably also be wanted) or just inline `matches!(dir, Directory::Bios(_))` at the two call sites. A trait inside an unrelated crate to add a one-line predicate is overhead with no payoff.

### 13. Snapshot fixtures hand-built, sidestep `psptool-fixtures::micro`'s composition surface
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/tests/list_micro.rs`
**Lines**: 14-70

Three near-identical `build_*_blob` helpers reach into `psptool_core::fet` constants and copy bytes by offset. The test crate imports `psptool_fixtures::micro` for `psp_directory()` / `bhd_directory()` but apparently the fixture crate doesn't yet provide a "synthetic 16 MiB blob with FET pointing at a directory at offset X." That's where the helper belongs — particularly given the comment "This mirrors the fixture in `psptool_core::directory::tests::synthetic_blob_with_psp_at`," confirming the third copy. Promote it.

## Closing Remarks

The shape is roughly right and the renderer compiles. But the column-content claims in the commit message ("matching the reference Python tool's column layout") are aspirational — the MD5 column is 4 characters of a 32-character digest, `subprogram` and `instance` are hex-formatted when the reference uses decimal, `destinationAddress` carries an extra `0x` prefix, the JSON entry-point lacks the verbose parameter the reference advertises, and the AGESA / signature / sha-verify cells emit `""` where the reference has actual placeholder strings. These are surface-level things that #18's differential test will catch eventually, but #10's stated scope is "matching reference column layout" — and the snapshot fixtures freeze the wrong values into perpetuity.

The code itself is reasonably tidy: small functions, clear separation between text and JSON renderers, table.rs is appropriately minimal. No I/O snuck in, no CLI binding leaked into the ops crate. So credit where due — but the contract this commit claims to honour is the one it's least careful with.

**Change**: `sopyspvl` — psptool-ops: list (default + verbose + json) [CL-10] (round 2 — post-fix verification)
**Date**: 2026-05-09
**Verdict**: Begrudgingly Adequate

## Round-1 must-fix items: verification

### MAJOR 1 — body_md5_short → full 32-char MD5: **honest fix**
`body_md5_hex` now writes all 16 digest bytes via `write!(s, "{:02x}", b)` and pre-allocates 32 chars. The verbose snapshot shows `4ae71336e44bf9bf79d2752e234818a5` — full digest. Confirmed.

### MINOR 3 — destinationAddress bare hex, BIOS sentinel suppressed: **honest fix**
`format!("{:x}", b.destination)` emits bare hex (no `0x`). The BHD-micro fixture's 0xFFFF…FF sentinel is suppressed: the `list_json_bhd_micro.snap` has no `destinationAddress` key. Confirmed.

### MINOR 4 — Subprogram/Instance render as decimal: **honest fix**
`subprogram.to_string()` / `instance.to_string()` (Display on u8 → decimal). Snapshot shows `0` not `0x0`. Confirmed.

### MINOR 5 — pubkey magic returns certifying_id ASCII tag: **plausible fix**
`magic_id_string` falls through to pubkey path, takes `certifying_id[0..4]`, ASCII-or-hex. Reference is `PubkeyFile.get_readable_magic() == self.certifying_id.magic`. The fixer's reading of `.magic` as "leading 4 bytes" is consistent with how magic is structurally laid out everywhere else in the codebase. Not refutable without the corpus checkout — accepted.

### MINOR 6 — entries parsed once per directory; parse errors surface as placeholder rows: **honest fix**
`entries_for_directory` returns `Vec<EntryRow>`; `render_text` and `list_json` both call it once per directory and reuse. `build_error_row` and the JSON `error` arm both produce row-shaped output. Confirmed.

### MINOR 7 — combo gen all per-entry generations; PSP/BIOS render their zen_generation: **honest fix, with a minor caveat (see Issue 1 below)**
`directory_generation` for `Directory::Combo` deduplicates labels into "Zen2, Zen3" form. For PSP/BIOS it walks back via `DirectoryProvenance::ComboEntry { combo_offset, index }` to read the originating combo entry's `psp_generation.zen_generation()`. Confirmed.

### MINOR 8 — placeholder strings for unknown reference fields: **honest fix**
`AGESA_UNKNOWN`, `SIG_UNKNOWN`, `SHA_UNKNOWN` constants. Snapshot shows AGESA_UNKNOWN in the rom-summary table. Confirmed.

### MINOR 9 — ROM index parameterized via RomListing: **honest fix**
`pub index: usize` on `RomListing`; `render_rom_table` emits `rom.index.to_string()`. Confirmed.

### MINOR 10 — info ordering matches reference; double-add removed: **honest fix**
`info_list` collapses `bios_flag_compressed || header_compressed` into a single `compressed` token. Order: `compressed → signed → SIG_UNKNOWN → encrypted → sha256/sha384 → SHA_UNKNOWN → pubkey_usage → destination(...)`. Reasonable. Confirmed by inspection.

## New issues introduced by the fix

### 1. `directory_generation` is quadratic in `rom.directories.len()`
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 519-541

For every PSP/BIOS directory reached via a combo entry, we re-scan the entire `rom.directories` slice to find the originating combo by offset. On a combo blob with N directories, that's O(N²). Combo blobs are small (a handful of dirs) so this is irrelevant in practice, but it's the kind of code that becomes a gotcha when someone later passes a synthetic mega-blob. A `HashMap<FlashOffset, &ComboDirectory>` constructed once would cost ten lines and end the discussion. Not blocking — file it under "I noticed".

### 2. `destinationAddress` JSON key emitted only for type "BIOS", but `info` text emits `destination(...)` for both BIOS and APOB
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 317-325 vs. 462-466

`entry_to_json` gates the `destinationAddress` top-level key on `readable_type(...) == "BIOS"`. But `info_list` adds the `destination(<hex>)` token for both BIOS and APOB. If the reference's `ls_files_dict` is the source of truth and it emits the structured `destinationAddress` only for BIOS files, this is correct. If it emits it for APOB too, you've got a quiet divergence. Without the corpus checked out I cannot prove either direction. Flagging for whoever runs differential (#18) — either confirm against reference and add APOB, or add a comment explaining the asymmetry.

### 3. `version` and `magic` JSON fields emit `""` instead of `null` for entries lacking a header/pubkey class
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 421-426 (version_string), 396-414 (magic_id_string)

Empty string vs. `null` is the kind of thing JSON consumers care about — `if (entry.version)` behaves differently for `""` vs. `null`. Pythonic reference dicts often use `None` (→ JSON `null`). Possibly fine, possibly a divergence. Differential testing in #18 will catch it. Not worth fixing speculatively.

### 4. `pubkey_usage` only names `key_usage == 0`
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 481-486

Everything that isn't 0 falls through to `key_usage(0x{x})`. The reference Python tool has a fuller table. Not a regression vs. round-1 — the round-1 review didn't flag it. Acceptable as a follow-up.

## Closing Remarks

I came in expecting the fixer to have papered over half the round-1 list with one-line band-aids. They didn't. The MAJOR items are fixed cleanly: the MD5 is genuinely 32 chars (verified in the snapshot, not just claimed), `list_json` takes `verbose` and the verbose snapshot exercises both branches, the BIOS sentinel is suppressed in the JSON snapshot.

The MINOR items are handled with appropriate skepticism: parse errors propagate as placeholder rows instead of being silently dropped, the combo→child generation lookup uses `DirectoryProvenance` (which means a new field had to be threaded through `psptool-core`, which the fixer also did — see the `pub use` of `DirectoryProvenance`), and the info ordering doesn't double-emit `compressed`.

Tests pass (21/21, including 7 snapshot tests that actually encode the corrected invariants). Build is clean. No new unsafe casts, no new panics, no new TODO/HACK/FIXME.

It physically pains me to write this, but the fix is honest. The remaining issues are genuinely follow-ups, not "fixes that didn't fix". Differential testing (#18) will be the real judge — that's where the JSON-shape vs. reference-Python questions get resolved.

**Must-fix count: 0. Follow-up suggestions: 4 (all Minor or Nitpick).**

### 6. `entries_for_directory` re-parses entries on every call
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 86-97, 143-186, 283-311

```rust
fn render_text(rom: &RomListing<'_>, verbose: bool) -> String {
    [...]
    for (idx, dir_ref) in rom.directories.iter().enumerate() {
        [...]
        out.push_str(&render_directory_header_table(idx, dir, rom));
        out.push_str(&render_entries_table(rom, dir, verbose));
        [...]
    }
}
```

`render_directory_header_table` calls `secondary_addresses` (which iterates `dir.entries`); `render_entries_table` then calls `entries_for_directory` which re-parses every PSP/BIOS entry from scratch via `Entry::parse_psp` / `Entry::parse_bios`. The same parse work happens again in `list_json`. Issue #10's `RomListing` already takes parsed `DirectoryRef`s — it's odd that the rest of the parsing then happens lazily, twice, in the renderer. Parse once, then render. Or parse in `walk_directories`'s output (a different issue's job, sure). At minimum don't re-parse for the second renderer call inside `render_text`.

Errors from `Entry::parse_psp` / `Entry::parse_bios` are also silently swallowed (`if let Ok(e) = ...`), which means a malformed entry in a parseable directory disappears from `ls` output with no indication. The Python tool surfaces these via the `PrintHelper` warnings infrastructure; the Rust port at least owes the user a placeholder row.

### 7. Combo directory generation hack
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 425-437

```rust
fn directory_generation(dir: &Directory) -> String {
    if let Directory::Combo(c) = dir {
        if let Some(first) = c.entries.first()
            && let Some(g) = first.psp_generation.zen_generation()
        {
            return format!("{:?}", g);
        }
    }
    String::new()
}
```

Two problems: (a) the function only ever returns a non-empty string for combo directories, but PSPTool's `ls` displays the per-directory `zen_generation` for `$PSP`/`$BHD` directories too (it's stored on `Directory.zen_generation`). So PSP/BIOS directories get an empty `Generation` cell when they shouldn't. (b) For combos, picking the first entry's generation and calling it the directory's generation is an admitted hack — the comment even says so. Either render all of them (`"Zen2, Zen3"`) or document this divergence somewhere a future reader will find.

### 8. AGESA column lies through omission
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 99-110

```rust
t.add_row([
    "0".to_string(),
    format_hex_u64(rom.blob.offset().get()),
    format_hex_u64(rom.blob.len() as u64),
    format_hex_u64(rom.fet.source.offset().get()),
    // AGESA-version extraction is not yet wired up in psptool-core.
    String::new(),
]);
```

The commit message says "explicit follow-ups, not stubs" — fine, but the user-visible result is a column reading "AGESA" with an empty cell, indistinguishable from "this ROM has no AGESA string." `'AGESA_UNKNOWN'` would at least match what the reference Python tool emits when extraction fails. As-is the empty cell is a UX silent failure mode.

Same applies to `version_string`, signature-verify, sha-checksum-verify — all silently emit `""` rather than the reference's actual placeholder strings.

### 9. ROM index hard-coded to "0"
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 99-110

The ROM table emits `"0"` as the index unconditionally. PSPTool supports multi-ROM blobs (Naples/Rome dual-ROM images) — `Rom` is a real concept in the reference and `cli-surface.md` documents `--rom-index`. `RomListing` holds a single ROM and the function happily lies about its index. If `RomListing` is the per-ROM input, take an `index: usize` so the caller can supply it.

### 10. `info` ordering is the reverse of the reference
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 359-393

The Python `File.info` accumulator pushes flags in this order: `compressed`, `signed`, `encrypted`, then sha tags. Here the order is `compressed` (from BIOS flags), then if `Header`: `compressed`, `encrypted`, `signed`, then sha tags, then pubkey usage, then BIOS destination. The header path puts `encrypted` before `signed`; reference is `signed` before `encrypted`. Easy fix; matters because the joined `File Info` cell is part of the column-layout contract.

Also, BIOS+Header double-counts compressed: a `BiosFile` with a header (none exist in spec, but the code accommodates one by checking both `EntryRecord::Bios.is_compressed()` and `h.is_compressed`) would add `compressed` twice.

### 11. `magic_string(bytes)` is a one-line wrapper around `ascii_or_hex_4`
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 421-423

Pointless indirection. Inline the call site or delete the wrapper. There is precisely one caller.

### 12. `DirectoryExt` trait extends a type you own
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/list.rs`
**Lines**: 503-511

```rust
trait DirectoryExt {
    fn is_bios(&self) -> bool;
}

impl DirectoryExt for Directory {
    fn is_bios(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Directory::Bios(_))
    }
}
```

`Directory` is in `psptool-core`. Either upstream the helper into core (where `is_psp`/`is_combo` will inevitably also be wanted) or just inline `matches!(dir, Directory::Bios(_))` at the two call sites. A trait inside an unrelated crate to add a one-line predicate is overhead with no payoff.

### 13. Snapshot fixtures hand-built, sidestep `psptool-fixtures::micro`'s composition surface
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/tests/list_micro.rs`
**Lines**: 14-70

Three near-identical `build_*_blob` helpers reach into `psptool_core::fet` constants and copy bytes by offset. The test crate imports `psptool_fixtures::micro` for `psp_directory()` / `bhd_directory()` but apparently the fixture crate doesn't yet provide a "synthetic 16 MiB blob with FET pointing at a directory at offset X." That's where the helper belongs — particularly given the comment "This mirrors the fixture in `psptool_core::directory::tests::synthetic_blob_with_psp_at`," confirming the third copy. Promote it.

## Closing Remarks

The shape is roughly right and the renderer compiles. But the column-content claims in the commit message ("matching the reference Python tool's column layout") are aspirational — the MD5 column is 4 characters of a 32-character digest, `subprogram` and `instance` are hex-formatted when the reference uses decimal, `destinationAddress` carries an extra `0x` prefix, the JSON entry-point lacks the verbose parameter the reference advertises, and the AGESA / signature / sha-verify cells emit `""` where the reference has actual placeholder strings. These are surface-level things that #18's differential test will catch eventually, but #10's stated scope is "matching reference column layout" — and the snapshot fixtures freeze the wrong values into perpetuity.

The code itself is reasonably tidy: small functions, clear separation between text and JSON renderers, table.rs is appropriately minimal. No I/O snuck in, no CLI binding leaked into the ops crate. So credit where due — but the contract this commit claims to honour is the one it's least careful with.

# The Hater's Code Review

**Change**: `b3685db` — psptool-cli: argv + subcommand dispatch [CL-15]
**Date**: 2026-05-09
**Verdict**: Sloppy

## Issues

### 1. `verify` always exits 0, even when entries fail verification
**Severity**: Critical
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/verify.rs`
**Lines**: 12–29

`run` builds the report, prints it, and returns `Ok(())` unconditionally. There is no inspection of `EntryVerification::status`, no failure tally, nothing. A ROM where every signed entry fails verification exits with code 0 and a happy little stdout dump. The kickoff prompt explicitly lists "Exit codes wrong (e.g., 0 on a verify-failed case the reference exits non-zero on)" as a VALID critique, and you walked right into it.

Fix: scan the report; if any row is not `verified` / `not-signed`, return a non-zero exit. Or be principled and let the caller pick the policy via `--strict`, but the *default* must not be "shrug, it's all fine."

### 2. `-E -m` (metrics) output is fabricated, not the reference format
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/list.rs`
**Lines**: 25–28, 57–71

Spec §1.3 / §2.2: `-m` calls `psp.print_metrics()` — filename + error/warning/info counts + rom/directory/unique-file counts. Your `write_metrics` emits `directories: N`, `entries: N`, `rom_size: 0x…`. None of those keys match. None of those values overlap. Any pre-existing script that greps `print_metrics` output will break. This is a drop-in compat failure on a specifically-listed flag.

Either implement the real metrics surface or rip the flag out. Lying about implementing it is the worst option.

### 3. `-E -t` (key-tree) silently emits a placeholder string
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/list.rs`
**Lines**: 15–24

When the user passes `-t`, you print "key-tree printing is not yet implemented" and **exit 0**. A script that pipes the key tree to a grep gets a successful exit, no key tree, and no diagnostic on stderr. The minimum acceptable behavior is a non-zero exit with the message on stderr; the correct behavior is implementing the flag or removing it entirely.

### 4. `-E -n` is silently swallowed (compat lie)
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/list.rs`
**Lines**: 39–43

Spec §1.3: `-E -n` should call `ls_files()` — a flat unique-files listing. Your implementation literally has `let _ = args.no_duplicates;` with a comment saying "existing callers that pass `-n` get the standard listing, never an error." That is the textbook definition of a drop-in compatibility break: the flag is accepted, advertised as supported in `--help`, and produces *the wrong output*. Worse than a removed flag, because it fails silently.

### 5. Single-file `-X -c` calls the wrong function (asymmetry not preserved)
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/extract.rs`
**Lines**: 125–139, 161–172

`docs/cli-surface.md` §2.10 explicitly warns that single-file `-c` must call `to_decrypted_file_bytes()` (clears encrypted-bit + IV, body decrypted, signature preserved) while multi-file `-c` must call `get_decrypted_body()` (just the decrypted body). Your `transform_single` and the multi-file loop both call `extract_decrypted` with the same Ikek. Same function, both modes. The asymmetry the doc explicitly says to preserve is gone.

### 6. Multi-file extract filenames don't follow the spec
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/extract.rs`
**Lines**: 158–190

Spec §1.7 mandates filename rules: append `_SUB_{hex}_INS_{hex}` if subprogram/instance non-zero; append `_{readable_version}` for `HeaderFile`; for `-n` mode the path is `outdir/{readable_type}[_{readable_version}]`. You write `d{NN}_e{NN}_{TYPE}` (no SUB/INS, no version) or `{TYPE}` for `-n` (no version). On a real ROM this collapses entries with the same type but different (subprogram, instance) onto the same path — silent file overwrites during multi-file extraction.

### 7. Multi-file extract babbles to stdout
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/extract.rs`
**Lines**: 49

`writeln!(out, "wrote entries to {}", outdir.display())?` — upstream `-X` writes binary to stdout/files and is silent on success. Your decoration breaks any caller who pipes single-file `-X` to stdout in a way the user might script around (you don't; only `outfile`-mode does this, but the `replace`/`sign` commands also chatter — see #8).

### 8. `replace` and `sign` print success chatter to stdout
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/replace.rs`, `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/sign.rs`
**Lines**: replace.rs:63–68, 81–86; sign.rs:25–30

`"wrote N bytes to PATH"` on stdout. Upstream `-R` writes the ROM to `outfile` and is silent. If anything, that line belongs on stderr. Trivial, but every chatty CLI has a thousand little decisions like this.

### 9. `-V` version output diverges from upstream
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/main.rs`
**Lines**: 44–53

Upstream prints `psptool.__version__` (a single version string). You print `psptool X.Y.Z (psptool-core X.Y.Z, psptool-ops X.Y.Z)`. Scripts that parse `psptool -V | awk '{print $2}'` still work; scripts that grep the entire line break. Reasonable engineering choice, but it *is* a drop-in compat divergence and the commit message claims "drop-in flag compatibility … keeps working unchanged."

### 10. `--privkeystub` renamed to `--privkey` (canonical form changed)
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cli.rs`
**Lines**: 118, 244, 273

Spec §1.4: upstream long form is `--privkeystub`. You made `--privkey` the canonical and demoted `--privkeystub` to a `visible_alias`. Calls work either way today, but `psptool --help` documents the *new* name as canonical; help-scraping tools see the wrong canonical. Either keep `--privkeystub` as the long form or make a deliberate, documented rename — don't half-do it.

### 11. `nth(rom_index)` over a `filter_map` silently mis-indexes
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/load.rs`
**Lines**: 38–47

`candidates.iter().filter_map(...).nth(rom_index)` skips FET candidates whose layout detection fails. So a blob with three FET candidates where candidate[0] fails detection and the user passes `--rom-index 1` gets candidate[2]'s ROM — *not* the second ROM out of two valid ones (which is what the user might expect), but also *not* the second FET candidate (which is what the error message implies: "ROM index 1 out of range (found 3 ROM(s))"). The error message lies about what `rom_index` even indexes against.

Either make `rom_index` index the candidate list (and report layout-detection failures separately) or filter first and report the *filtered* count in the error. Picking neither is just confusing.

### 12. `-T` regex match over re-parsed entries discards parse errors
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/extract.rs`
**Lines**: 222–238

`for_each_entry` swallows every `Entry::parse_*` error with `if let Ok(entry) = …`. A corrupt entry index is invisible; the regex match silently doesn't see entries that fail to parse. If `-T` finds zero matches because ten entries failed to parse, the user gets "no entry matches type regex …" with no clue why. At minimum log the parse failures to stderr.

### 13. `extract` multi-file path sanitizer is naive
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/extract.rs`
**Lines**: 257–267

`sanitize_for_path` filters `/`, `\`, and control chars. It does *not* filter `..`. A `readable_type` that resolves to `..` (won't happen with current `psp_name` table, but the function takes arbitrary strings) lets the constructed path escape `outdir`. Defense-in-depth: also reject paths containing `..` segments after `Path::new(stem).components()`.

### 14. `help.rs` snapshot test is decoupled from the actual binary
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/tests/help.rs`
**Lines**: 15–27

`#[path = "../src/cli.rs"] mod cli;` re-imports `cli.rs` as a test-local module, then calls `Cli::command()`. That guards the `cli.rs` surface, sure — but `main.rs` could grow flag handling that diverges from `cli.rs`'s declared surface and the snapshot would never notice. The whole point of snapshotting `--help` per #15 is to lock the *binary's* output. Either run the actual binary with `Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_psptool"))` (which `synthetic.rs` already does), or document why the indirection is acceptable.

### 15. Sign / replace ignore the `--privkeypass` argument
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/sign.rs`, `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/replace.rs`
**Lines**: cli.rs:247–250, 276–278; load_priv_key uses unencrypted PEM only

The CLI accepts `-a/--privkeypass`, the doc-comment says "currently ignored — `rsa::pkcs8::DecodePrivateKey` reads PEM directly; encrypted-PEM support is a follow-up." So if a user passes `-a hunter2` against an encrypted PEM, the parse fails inside `from_pkcs8_pem`, the password is silently ignored, and the error message is about PKCS8 parsing — not "encrypted PEMs not supported, drop the password and use an unencrypted key." Either reject `-a` outright with a clear error, or implement it. Accepting it as a no-op is the worst of both worlds.

### 16. `BlobEditor::from_blob(opened.blob.clone())` — full ROM clone per replace
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/replace.rs`
**Lines**: 22, 53–58

You clone the entire `SourceBytes` into the editor, then for the re-sign path build a *second* `SourceBytes` from `editor.serialize()` and a *third* `BlobEditor` over that. Three full-ROM allocations for one replace+sign. Acceptable for a multi-megabyte ROM, but it's wasteful and the comment doesn't acknowledge it.

## Closing Remarks

The shape is right — clap derive, anyhow at the bin layer, snapshot tests on help, subcommand dispatch wired to `psptool-ops`. The legacy action flags are accepted at the top level, which is the hardest piece to get right. Credit there.

But the commit message claims "drop-in flag compatibility … pre-existing scripts keep working unchanged" and that claim is false in at least four concrete ways: `-m` produces a different format, `-n` is silently swallowed, `-t` returns a placeholder string with exit 0, and `-V` output diverges. The `verify` subcommand exits 0 on failure, which the kickoff prompt explicitly named as a VALID critique. The single/multi-file `-c` asymmetry the design doc *specifically* called out is gone. Multi-file extraction will silently overwrite files when subprogram/instance differ.

This is what happens when you write the help text first and the behavior second. Fix the verify exit code today; fix the metrics/key-tree/no-duplicates lies before this lands.

# The Hater's Code Review

**Change**: `2aceec8` (round-1 fixer atop `b3685db`) — psptool-cli round-2 fixes for #15
**Date**: 2026-05-09
**Verdict**: Begrudgingly Adequate

## Issues

### 1. New `-m` / extract-suffix code is untested
**Severity**: Major
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/tests/synthetic.rs`
**Lines**: n/a — *absence* of tests

The fixer claims byte-exact parity with upstream `print_metrics()` and upstream `__main__.py:202-209` suffix logic, then ships zero snapshot tests for either. The 13 passing CLI tests are the same 13 from round 1 — none touch `-m`, none touch multi-file extract, none cover sub/ins/version suffix collisions. "Format parity" claims with no fixture is a regression waiting to happen the moment someone refactors the f-string output.

### 2. `unique_files_count` re-walks the whole blob from scratch
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/list.rs`
**Lines**: 84-100

`write_metrics` calls `scan_fet_candidates` + `detect_rom_layout` + `walk_directories` *again* even though `open_rom` already produced an `OpenedRom` with parsed directories for `args.rom_index`. For a single-ROM blob (the common case) you parse everything twice. Fine for an 8 MiB synthetic; less fine for the 64 MiB corpus images. Either reuse `opened.directories` for the selected ROM, or document why a from-scratch rescan is required (combo blobs?). Right now it's neither.

### 3. `Directory::Combo` silently contributes nothing to `unique_files_count`
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/list.rs`
**Lines**: 130-134

`collect_unique_bodies` matches `Combo(_) => {}`. If upstream's `unique_files()` recurses into combo directories' children (it does), this undercounts on combo ROMs. Either recurse, or leave a `// TODO recurse combo children` so the next reader knows it's a known gap, not an oversight.

### 4. `header_version_suffix` reads bytes by index without bounds proof
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/extract.rs`
**Lines**: 234-244

`header.version.iter().rev()` is fine *iff* `version` is a fixed-size `[u8; 4]`. If it's ever a `Vec<u8>` of arbitrary length the suffix silently changes shape. A type-level `[u8; 4]` would make this self-evident; if it already is, no action.

### 5. Verify-failure error message is presentational, not structured
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-cli/src/cmds/verify.rs`
**Lines**: 44-52

`bail!("{N} of {M} entr{y/ies} failed...")` returns through anyhow, which means the exit message goes to stderr with the rest of the binary's error chain prefix. Functional, but a dedicated `process::exit(1)` after writing a structured one-liner would be cleaner for the "CI parses our exit code" use case the commit message specifically calls out. Not blocking.

## Closing Remarks

Round-1 must-fixes 1-5 all landed honestly: verify exits non-zero on real failures, `-m` matches the upstream f-string set (modulo zero-stubbed PrintHelper counters, which is documented), `-t` and `-n` bail loudly instead of lying, and the multi-file extract suffix logic mirrors the cited Python lines. Tests pass, no clippy regressions visible. The one thing that genuinely irritates me is shipping format-parity claims with no test that would catch them drifting — that's the kind of debt that bites in six months. Fix the test gap and this is fine work. As is, it's *adequate*.

# Hater review: #7 — psptool-core entry parser + entry-kind taxonomy

## Verdict
NITS-ONLY

## Must-fix
(none)

## Nits (optional)

- `crates/psptool-core/src/entry.rs:316-319` and `:535-539` — the
  `EntryClass::KeyStore(HeaderEntry)` branch reuses the generic PSP
  signed-entry header parser for `0x50/0x51` keystore bodies. PSPTool's
  `KeyStoreFileHeader` (`vendor/.../key_store_file.py:74-89`) overlaps the PSP
  HeaderFile only at the signature-fingerprint slot. Critical fields differ:
  `+0x14` is `body_size` (not `size_signed`), `+0x6c` is `packed_size` (not
  `rom_size`), `+0x7c` is `keystore_type`. A caller reading
  `keystore.0.size_signed` will get a value the field name lies about. The
  module docs claim "the leading PSP header is parsed; the embedded `$KDB`
  body is deferred". That sentence is a polite fiction — there is no leading
  PSP header on a keystore. Either: (a) gate the keystore-specific
  interpretation behind a separate `KeyStoreEntryHeader` struct (deferred to

  exists but is never wired into `parse()`. Comment says "we let callers

  raises on undocumented values (`header_file.py:128`). Pick a position:
  either expose this as a soft warning in the public API, or document
  loudly that this parser is more permissive than PSPTool. Right now the
  function looks like dead-but-public surface area.

- Field offsets in `HeaderEntry::parse` (lines 165-182) cross-checked
  against `vendor/.../psptool/header_file.py:42-57`: magic@0x10, size_signed@0x14,
  is_encrypted@0x18, iv@0x20-0x30, signed@0x30, signature_type@0x34,

  zlib_size@0x54, bitfield@0x58 (BIG-ENDIAN — confirmed `>I`), version@0x60-0x64,
  load_addr@0x68, rom_size@0x6c, wrapped_key@0x80-0x90. All correct.
- `PubkeyEntry::parse` (lines 273-281) cross-checked against
  `pubkey_file.py:61-76`: version@0x00, key_id@0x04-0x14, certifying_id@0x14-0x24,
  key_usage@0x24-0x28, security_features@0x2A-0x2C, pubexp_bits@0x38-0x3C,
  modulus_bits@0x3C-0x40. All correct.
- Classification ordering (lines 518-549) is functionally equivalent to
  `file.py:from_entry` (lines 249-272) for all defined entry types: no
  overlap between PUBKEY/KEYSTORE/SECONDARY/TERTIARY/SOFT_FUSE sets, so
  the up-front short-circuiting for the richer enum variants doesn't
  alter dispatch outcomes.
- `resolve_body` (lines 469-511) is bounds-safe: saturating_add on
  body_end, explicit `body_offset < blob_start` and `body_end > blob_end`
  checks, `slice(local, size)` with `checked_add` internally. No panic
  paths on malformed inputs, no unchecked indexing on attacker-controlled
  offsets. Unwrap on line 162 (`body.slice(0, HEADER_FILE_LEN).expect(...)`)
  is guarded by the preceding length check on the same `body`. Fine.
- Soft-fuse-chain handling (line 484, NO_SIZE entry type 0x0B) matches

- 19 tests, all green via `cargo test -p psptool-core --lib entry::`.

6c23d90d-6db6-43dc-90db-2154af41be59.description:
Replace an entry body, producing a new ROM image. Equivalent to the reference `replace` command — except this one does not corrupt unrelated bytes (which is the bug class fixed by https://github.com/PSPReverse/PSPTool/pull/77).

API:
```rust
let mut edit = blob.edit();
edit.entry_mut(target).set_body(new_bytes);
let new_rom = edit.serialize();
```

Required guarantees:
- Sibling entries: byte-identical to source.
- Padding bytes: byte-identical to source.
- Length and address fields in the entry header: rewritten correctly (no false 0x10-alignment assumption).
- If the new body is larger than the original AND would overflow an existing slot, return a typed error rather than silently corrupting neighbors.

# The Hater's Code Review

**Change**: `668a60f` — `psptool-ops: replace entry body [CL-12]`
**Date**: 2026-05-09
**Verdict**: Begrudgingly Adequate

I sat down expecting to find another author who had read the PSPTool PR-#77 thread and learned exactly the wrong lesson from it. I am, against my better judgment, mostly disappointed.

## Issues

### 1. Per-corpus-ROM test silently passes when the ROM has no replaceable entries
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/tests/corpus_replace.rs`
**Lines**: 147-153, 233-279

`first_replaceable` returns `None` if no `Entry::parse_psp` / `Entry::parse_bios` succeeds — `if let Ok(entry) = ...` deliberately swallows parse failures. `run_one` then treats `None` as legitimate ("empty / soft-fuse-only ROM") and returns `Ok(())`. A corpus ROM whose every reachable entry trips a parser bug will pass this test as a clean no-op rather than failing loudly. The corpus_roundtrip headline test catches the parse-level regression so the gap isn't fatal, but the comment "Empty / soft-fuse-only ROMs are legitimate" is doing more lifting than the code earns. At minimum log a "no replaceable entry found in N reachable directories" diagnostic so somebody investigating a flaky corpus run isn't fishing.

### 2. `replace_entry_body` accepts an `Entry` from any blob, fails far away
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/replace.rs`
**Lines**: 132-138

The doc comment notes that passing an `Entry` parsed against a different blob "lands at offsets that do not exist in the editor's source bytes (and are rejected as `PatchError::OutOfBounds`)" — fine, but if the offsets *happen* to be in-bounds in the editor's blob you'll silently corrupt unrelated bytes. The two helpers that re-parse the entry from `editor.original()` make the pre-parsed-Entry footgun the only unsafe-by-construction surface. A debug-assert that `entry.record.source().offset()` lies inside `editor.original().flash_range()` would close the gap for ~zero cost.

### 3. `apply()` records the size-field patch *before* validating the body patch
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/replace.rs`
**Lines**: 153-170

Comment says "either both succeed or neither commits" — that's only true today because `BlobEditor::patch` validates against `original` (not against the patch set's bounds, which the size patch couldn't violate anyway). It's true *by accident*. If someone later adds e.g. a "patches must respect a quota" rule to `BlobEditor::patch`, the size-field patch will land while the body patch fails, leaving the editor in an inconsistent state. Either build the patch list locally, validate, then commit atomically, or stop pretending in the comment.

### 4. The "0x10 alignment" docstring is stronger than the code
**Severity**: Nitpick
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/src/replace.rs`
**Lines**: 20-25

The docstring claims fix-by-construction for the PR-#77 class. The actual fix is "we use `new_body.len()` literally instead of rounding up". That's correct — but you should at least cite which test enforces it (`shrinking_rewrites_size_field_to_exact_length` uses 0x33 specifically for this). Without the test reference the comment reads like a mission statement; with it, it reads like a guarantee.

### 5. `Cargo.toml` adds `default = ["corpus"]`
**Severity**: Minor
**File**: `crates/psptool-ops/Cargo.toml`
**Lines**: 17-18

The corpus feature defaulting on means anyone building `psptool-ops` from a tree without the (315 MB private) submodule hydrated will… still build fine, because the runtime gate is `PSPTOOL_TEST_CORPUS`. So the feature default is harmless. But it's also pointless: the `corpus` feature only changes test behaviour, not the library, and it gates against a private submodule. CI lanes that explicitly want the no-corpus path now have to remember `--no-default-features`. Either justify the default or flip it off.

## Closing Remarks

I came in looking for the PR-#77 alignment-rounding bug, the directory-record-mode arithmetic mistake, the silently-clobbered sibling, and the silent-pass corpus harness. None of those are here. The implementation is roughly fifty lines of business logic layered on top of `BlobEditor::patch`, the size-field rewrite uses the entry record's already-resolved absolute flash offset (which means no address-mode arithmetic to get wrong — clever), and the corpus test mirrors the existing `corpus_roundtrip` SKIP_LIST infrastructure faithfully including the `Failed`-on-skip-list pattern that prevents `--include-ignored` from re-introducing a silent pass.

The unit tests target the right invariants: locality (only the body bytes change), exact non-aligned size rewrite (0x33, deliberately picked to fail any 0x10-rounding implementation), single-patch count for equal-length replacements, BIOS-family parity, soft-fuse-chain rejection, and growth rejection without dangling patches.

The remaining nits are all paperwork — diagnostics, doc precision, a defensive debug-assert. Nothing structural.

I refuse to give this an "Acceptable". Begrudgingly Adequate is the upgrade path you've earned. Do the cleanup; don't make me regret it.
